description_en: The stone memorial pillar is installed on the side of the path between Rārā lake (alt. 3000 m) and the village of Murmā (alt. 3250 m).Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors.The pillar is oriented to the east. Only its eastern side is decorated with carvings and contains an inscription. On the upper register are motifs representing the sun and the moon. Directly below is a star-shaped motif. The inscription, too eroded to allow any reading, occupies the central register.The monument is typologicaly close to pillars found in Rārā (MUG0080 and MUG0150) and in Lāhā (MUG0030). Two pillars from these sites (MUG0030-003 and MUG0150-003) are dated of 1404 of the Śaka era, which corresponds to 1482 CE. It is therefore very likely that the Kham Gaite was erected around the same time (late 15th century).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019.
